clips.hook_plain: Don't fail the bet you made
clips.notes: Guest: Andy, SoloLink (SaaS Gold winner, ~120 accounts) — confirm name/brand spelling.
clips.transcript: If you have one piece of advice for someone who is just starting out, maybe they have no customers, maybe they have one customer for their high level SaaS. What would you say is like the one thing that they've got to do in order to like get more customers and keep them and grow to be like a SaaS winner or award winner in the future? Man, the one thing. clips.title: You can do anything. Not everything.
clips.speaker: Andy + Andrew
clips.hook_q: Can you run an agency alone at 100 clients?
clips.notes: Guest: Andy, SoloLink (SaaS Gold winner, ~120 accounts) — confirm name/brand spelling.
clips.transcript: The saying that I've heard is, I can do anything, but I can't do everything. I know I did it. I think a lot of us get stuck in that kind of trap of trying to do everything. And it works when you get started. Like it does. Like there's nothing wrong with that when you get started. Like you can run an agency with your first five, 10 customers and do it all yourself. Easy. Easy. But yeah, well, I mean, once you're getting to 50, 60, 100 plus customers, yeah, it's impossible.

clips.title: Charge less at first. You're getting paid to learn.
clips.speaker: Andy
clips.hook_q: Should you charge less when you're starting out?
clips.notes: Guest: Andy, SoloLink (SaaS Gold winner, ~120 accounts) — confirm name/brand spelling.
clips.transcript: you may want to charge higher ticket prices for your services, but in the beginning, you have to eat a little bit of dirt, in my opinion, and maybe you have to go free or go low, but you're getting paid to learn. And that's, in my mind's eye, think of it as like, you know you want to do this anyways. If you can even offer it at a lower price than you normally would, you're getting paid to learn how to do it. And then you can earn the right privilege to charge what is the right amount for you and your services.
